recommendation: Confirm Q1, Q8, G3-G18, G3-HOSTILE, and G21-NT6. Amend G21-SCHEMA from six schema-dependent injections plus one fixture-form injection to five schema-dependent injections plus two fixture-form/raw-body injections: invalid UTF-8, like truncated bodies, is not blocked by a per-type body schema.
rationale: Independent remeasurement at HEAD f3b05e33479652ede37f0502084b50b590f630f7 confirmed the packet pins and Claude's corrected citations for five dispositions. Q1 is supported by signed-index-trust-contract.v14.json#$.namedOpenDecisions[2].standing, the eight live totalDecision entries, the incorporated C1 round-2 text, and D-314 item 5. Q8 is supported by component-manifest-schemas.v11.json#$.namedOpenDecisions[0], component-manifest-leftover-join.v15.json#$.obligations[9], and D-314 item 12; they support an evaluable later D-006-pattern method but no gate/corpus/runner triad. G3-G18 is supported by D-311's later-implementation-successor/P-1..P-8 rule, lifecycle-leftover-join.v4.json#$.proposedLaterWork[1..2], and the occupancy's quarantine reservation; the corrected failsIf attribution does not move the answer. G3-HOSTILE is supported by anti-lockstep-hostile-goldens.v3.json#$.classCoverage, #$.proposedLaterWork[2..3], and D-300: exactly the seven recorded class entries including CC-6 carry remainingNotAuthored. G21-NT6 is now an owner ruling in D-314 item 29 and its sequence matches DECISIONS-RECOMMENDED.md#B2; g21-leftover-join.v13.json still carries both #$.doesNot[20] and #$.obligations[3].remainingNotAuthored.dr133=["NT-6"], so Claude correctly preserves the counter-evidence and medium confidence on that reading. G21-SCHEMA does not survive. control-protocol-contract.v2.json#$.controlFrameEncoding.encoding requires UTF-8 before a JSON object can exist, #$.capabilityEnvelope.refusalFamilies.families[1].covers assigns invalid UTF-8 directly to RF-2, and #$.controlFrameEncoding.messageEnvelope applies only to a frame body object. An invalid-UTF-8 body therefore cannot reach type dispatch or any per-type body schema. The live CC-5 intent expressly includes invalid UTF-8, so this is not the rejected non-object-top-level classification. Moving invalid UTF-8 off the schema trigger changes when that member can be released; it is a disposition change, not a harmless citation correction.
refutations: Claude's G21-SCHEMA claim that all six listed injections need a complete body object is false for invalid UTF-8. The governing encoding rejects those bytes before a JSON object, type member, or per-type body can exist.

The D1-plan statement grouping seven injections as body-requiring does not establish that all seven require a per-type schema. control-protocol-contract.v2 separates raw frame-body decoding from message-envelope and per-type validation, and its RF-2 table names invalid UTF-8 independently.

Claude's top-level claim that none of its corrections changes an answer is therefore false: the invalid-UTF-8 member must move from the schema trigger to the recorded OQ-G21-4 fixture-form/raw-body question.
amendments: Replace the G21-SCHEMA six-and-one split with five-and-two: duplicate members, unknown members, floats, negative integers, and over-uint53 integers remain on the per-type-schema trigger; truncated bodies and invalid UTF-8 remain on OQ-G21-4's fixture-form/raw-body trigger and are not schema-blocked.
Retain every other D-314 disposition and Claude's non-load-bearing citation corrections.

perQuestion.recommendation: Keep the existing preview refusal as the decided OD-112-3 standing, retain OD-112-3 in namedOpenDecisions with an explicit DECIDED standing, and do not widen the policy beyond the preview product stage without a separate owner act.

Leave the OD-1 numeric limb explicitly open and supply no cap values. A later value proposal must state an evaluable measurement method and follow the recorded product-owned D-006 pattern without creating a gate/corpus/runner prerequisite here.

Leave G18 blocked, specify no quarantine format now, and do not permit quarantine fate without the bytes required by the closed-type rule. Use a reviewed later implementation successor that chooses the mechanism and proves the recorded P-1..P-8 properties, together with the other recorded type dependencies, as the lawful trigger.

Treat the citation-witness floor as already authored at D-300, leave the seven live v3 within-class universal sets including CC-6 named-open, and supply no per-class totals. A mechanical join remasurement may proceed under D-293's existing delegation if it adds no semantic choice; the cross-row byte-sharing question remains separate owner work.

Leave five injections named-open on the per-type-schema trigger: CC-5 duplicate members, unknown members, floats, negative integers, and over-uint53 integers. Keep CC-5 truncated bodies and invalid UTF-8 separately named-open on OQ-G21-4's fixture-form/raw-body trigger; do not classify either as schema-blocked.
refutations: control-protocol-contract.v2.json#$.controlFrameEncoding.encoding says a frame body is first decoded as UTF-8 JSON, while #$.controlFrameEncoding.messageEnvelope governs a frame body object. Invalid UTF-8 fails before that object and its type/per-type body schema can exist.

control-protocol-contract.v2.json#$.capabilityEnvelope.refusalFamilies.families[1].covers and #$.hostileDualChannelConformance.classes[4].intent both name invalid UTF-8 directly, so removing its schema dependency does not repeat the rejected inference from RF-2 membership to CC-5 membership.
Claude's asserted exact six-and-one partition is therefore wrong even after its truncated-body condition: invalid UTF-8 is the second raw framing/representation member, not a per-type-schema member.
amendments: Move CC-5 invalid UTF-8 from part (i) to part (ii), yielding five schema-trigger members and two OQ-G21-4 fixture-form/raw-body members.
Delete the claim that every member remaining in Claude's six-item list needs a complete body object.
